title: Mesoscopic mechanical superpositions by gluing individual quantum systems
abstract: We propose a protocol for preparing mechanical Schrödinger kittens -- mesoscopic quantum superpositions of coherent motional states of an optically levitated nanoparticle -- by adhering single electron time-bin states to its surface. Over short protocol timescales, coherence of the mesoscopic superposition survives the dominant decoherence mechanisms afflicting levitated systems, and can be observed by varying the phase of the time-bin electrons. Interference fringes can be detected with real-time, near-Heisenberg limited interferometry of photons scattered from the particle. This approach eliminates the need for coherent state expansion, dark potentials, and particle release-and-recapture mechanisms, providing a new route to test quantum mechanics in unprecedented scales.
summary: The paper details a method to create mechanical Schrödinger cat states in an optically levitated nanoparticle by coupling it to the momentum kicks from single electrons. By controlling the phase of these electron time-bin states, high-visibility interference fringes are generated, allowing for tests of quantum mechanics on unprecedentedly large objects while mitigating common decoherence sources.
main_problem: The authors propose a novel protocol to prepare and observe mesoscopic quantum superpositions of mechanical motion (Schrödinger kittens) in an optically levitated nanoparticle.
main_result: They demonstrate that coherence can be maintained over single oscillation periods by coupling the particle's state to controllable, phase-dependent momentum kicks imparted by single electrons. This method bypasses limitations of previous techniques for testing quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
method: The protocol involves using time-bin states of single electrons to induce a superposition of momentum kicks ($\pm \delta p$) onto the levitated nanoparticle, followed by interferometric measurement of the particle's position probability distribution.
model_or_system: The system is an amorphous $	ext{SiO}_2$ bead trapped in a harmonic potential. The quantum dynamics are analyzed using master equations and Wigner/characteristic functions to track decoherence from sources like gas collisions and trap fluctuations.
key_observables: Interference fringes in the particle's Center-of-Mass (CoM) position probability $P_{\Delta x}(\phi, x)$, non-classicality confirmed by Wigner negativity, and interference visibility ($V$).
important_parameters: The momentum kick $\delta p$ is controlled via external electric fields; decoherence rates ($\Gamma$) are compared against the trap frequency ($\omega$), with timescales set relative to the oscillation period ($\pi/\omega$).
main_assumptions: It assumes that the state preparation time ($\delta t$) is short enough such that harmonic motion and decoherence can be treated as approximately frozen during the kick application.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the interference pattern $P_{\Delta x}(\phi, x)$ varying sinusoidally with electron phase $\phi$, show Wigner function negativity for non-classical states, and plot visibility dependence on initial occupation number and decoherence rate.
paper_structure: The paper develops from proposing the protocol using time-bin electrons to induce momentum superpositions. It mathematically models the evolution of the quantum state (using master equations/Wigner functions) while analyzing various sources of decoherence, culminating in predictions for observable interference fringes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions about quantum mechanics at the mesoscopic scale by providing a robust experimental pathway that leverages single-particle interactions to manipulate macroscopic quantum states, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum sensing.
